# The Year We Stopped Shipping Sideways

January went badly. [Checkout] fell over on the 14th and stayed down for nine hours, and the cause turned out to be a retry loop one of us wrote in 2023 that had been quietly hammering our own primary database every time latency crept above a threshold nobody remembered setting. That outage set the agenda for the rest of the year.

Q1 was cleanup. We tore out the retry logic, put real circuit breakers in front of [payments] and [inventory], and wrote the first runbooks this team has ever had. Boring work. It moved p99 from [840ms to 210ms] and dropped on-call pages from [61 a month to 9].

The surprise was how much of that came from deletion. We removed [31,000 lines] this year — two dead feature flags, an entire caching layer that predated [Redis], and the admin panel three people used. Less code, fewer places to be wrong.

Not everything landed. The [Postgres 16] migration stalled in August when we hit the extension incompatibility, and it's still sitting in a branch. We under-scoped it, plainly. [Sam] and [Priya] joined in the spring and have been carrying the [billing] rewrite since June.

Next year I want us to get better at the thing we're worst at: saying no early. Half of what we deleted in Q1 was work we agreed to in a meeting where nobody wanted to be the one objecting.

Thanks for a good year. See you in January.
